page: Microsoft Azure E64ps_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft's ARM-based Neoverse-N2 processor architecture. It provides 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running at a clock frequency of 3.4 GHz. The instance is configured with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation, and includes 128 MB of shared L3 cache alongside 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core. There is no integrated local storage or GPU accelerator attached to this configuration, requiring attached remote block volumes for persistent disk storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant multi-threaded throughput and memory subsystem capacity. In multi-core assessments, the instance achieved top-tier rankings in stress-ng multi-core testing, Geekbench multi-core evaluations, and software compilation via Clang. Memory performance is equally prominent, posting top-tier scores in PassMark memory testing, large-block read operations at 465.5 GB/sec, and write operations at 203.88 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect average performance, as indicated by median scores across single-core Geekbench and stress-ng runs.

Due to its non-hyperthreaded 64-core density and 512.0 GB memory capacity, the E64ps_v6 delivers strong cost efficiency for scale-out parallel computing and memory-bound jobs rather than workloads constrained by single-thread frequency. The architecture is well matched for large in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, multi-threaded continuous integration and build pipelines, and high-throughput web serving environments.
description: Microsoft Azure E64ps_v6 is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by 64 dedicated ARM Neoverse-N2 physical cores operating at 3.4 GHz. Paired with 512.0 GB of system memory, it delivers an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio along with 128 MB of L3 cache. The instance features no local storage or onboard GPUs, relying entirely on networked storage volumes. In synthetic benchmarks, the E64ps_v6 demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded compute throughput, fast software compilation, and high memory bandwidth reaching 465.5 GB/sec for uncached reads and 203.88 GB/sec for uncached writes. While single-thread execution rates remain in the average tier, its dedicated core architecture eliminates thread contention. This profile offers robust cost efficiency and processing stability for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including in-memory databases, large Redis deployments, distributed build systems, and scalable web serving.
